descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Numbers — Reading, Composing, Comparing, Counting, and Sharing Numbers to 50, with Halves and Fourths (B1.1–B1.8)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Grade-1 unit on Numbers (B1.1-B1.8), framed around Lila the Button Collector, Otto the Marble Counter, and Scoot the puppy mascot. Estimation, multi-representation, compose/decompose, compare/order, fair-sharing, and unit fractions all in one focused week.
long_description: Children spend a focused week becoming Junior Number Friends — estimating, reading, composing, comparing, sharing, and seeing fractions as they really are. Day 1 'Count Big with Lila' opens with the estimation button jar and skip-counting on the Number Line floor mat (B1.4, B1.5). Day 2 'Read and Show Numbers' is a gallery walk where the same numbers appear in 5 forms — numerals, words, ten-frames, base-ten rods, tally marks (B1.1). Day 3 'Make and Break 50' is the keystone: composing and decomposing numbers in multiple ways, with the rod-moving demo to break the single-strategy trap (B1.2). Day 4 'Compare and Order' uses the Number Line classroom to anchor tens-first reasoning, with explicit work on the same-tens-look-at-ones rule (B1.3). Day 5 'Fair Shares — Halves and Fourths' is the capstone: fair-sharing rounds with leftovers (B1.6), the pizza-overlay reveal that 1/2 = 2/4 (B1.7), and unit fraction comparison up to 1/8 with the bigger-bottom-smaller-piece misconception explicitly addressed (B1.8). Each lesson includes a 4000+ char expanded_walkthrough covering 3 misconceptions paired with concrete recovery moves; mid-unit and end-of-unit assessments included.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans with 50-minute durations and 235 minutes of total teaching time
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson with name/date fields and child-voice learning goals
1 mid-unit formative assessment (Numerals 0-50 Check-In) administered between Lessons 3 and 4

10 printable teacher manipulatives: button card set, estimation jar template, base-ten rod label, Number Line floor mat (11 letter pages), pizza fraction cards, sharing paper plates, number-word match cards, and three character puppets (Lila, Otto, Scoot)
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 self-assessment prompts
1 eight-row summative rubric covering B1.1-B1.8 across 4 levels
1 summative-administration guide tying the rubric to Lesson 5 worksheet
Junior Number Friend certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony
Detailed expanded walkthroughs for every lesson including the rod-moving demo for the single-strategy decomposition trap and the pizza-overlay demo for the bigger-bottom-smaller-piece misconception
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
target_buyer: Ontario Grade 1 teachers covering the B1.1-B1.8 cluster of the 2026 Grade 1 Math curriculum. Useful as a 5-day unit at the start of the calendar year (September-October) or as a numbers-and-fractions review block in late winter before the report-card cycle.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression across the 5 days. Real buttons, base-ten rods, and pizza fractions anchor every concept before any worksheet abstraction. The keystone Lesson 3 uses the rod-moving demo to break single-strategy decomposition; the capstone Lesson 5 uses the pizza-overlay to break bigger-bottom-bigger-piece. Differentiation is proactive (built into every lesson) rather than remedial.
